description: snippets/SPEC.md fixes mcp_call's DEFAULT idempotency at requires_compensation. The default is the handler FLOOR: a snippet may declare a stricter tier, never a weaker one, so a floor above the contract's default silently removes the author's ability to declare the tier the contract allows.
notes: The default is the handler's DECLARED tier, and declaring the strictest one where the contract says compensable is not a safe over-approximation: the strictest tier is absolute, so it makes the contract's own default undeclarable. A workflow whose mcp_call step the author marked compensable then runs as if they had not, and a failed run reports final_state failed where the oracle reports rolled_back. MCP says nothing about whether a tool writes, so the strictest answer was a guess made on the author's behalf.
